message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to very different mammalian lineages—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively.  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of those two orders, which lived roughly **50–60 million years ago** during the early Eocene. This ancestor was a small, generalized mammal that gave rise to the diverse clade Laurasiatheria, from which both the carnivores and the odd‑toed ungulates eventually evolved.
